reasoning_traces.think:
This work formalizes a zero-sum adversarial game between a Chooser and Guesser over a directed graph, where payoffs depend on out-degrees and correctness of guesses. The core operators involve value propagation on trees and fans, yielding optimal strategies via inverse-weighted probabilities. These strategies are derived using Markov chain theory and linear algebraic methods such as matrix inversion and eigenvalue decomposition. The failure mode arises when terminal values collapse or when the graph lacks strong connectivity, rendering the optimal policies invalid. The model does not support GSE’s fixed-odds market framework due to its adversarial nature and payoff structure. It also lacks empirical validation or estimation techniques relevant to sports intelligence applications.
